title: Introducing a Voluntary Exit Offer
body: Introducing a Voluntary Exit Offer Oct 26, 2026 | Amy Coleman - Executive Vice President, Chief People Officer Amy Coleman, Executive Vice President and Chief People Officer, shared the below communication with Microsoft employees today. Today, we’re introducing a new Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) to eligible employees within participating organizations. This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support. It also gives participating organizations another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs. The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we’re evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter. This builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program. What employees should know This offer will be available to eligible employees in participating teams in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States at level 70 and below . This is a time-limited, voluntary program that gives those who are eligible the opportunity to leave Microsoft with financial support and career planning resources. Some organizations are providing the Voluntary Exit Offer, and some are not. Participation varies based on each business’s priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs. Eligible employees will receive an email with a link to their Voluntary Exit Offer details within the next few hours. Looking ahead The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us. We’ll learn from it. At the same time, we’ll keep helping people focus on the work that matters most, build new skills and, where it makes sense, find new opportunities across Microsoft. There is no one-size-fits-all approach for every team or every employee. These are a few of the ways we’re trying to meet different business needs while continuing to create opportunities for our own people to grow and contribute. My promise is to continue to provide clarity, listen and learn and keep improving. Thank you for everything you continue to do for our customers, Microsoft and for one another. Amy This Viva Engage post has been edited slightly for external use.

title: AWS Weekly Roundup: Amazon Polly Generative engine, TorchNeuron for Trainium, and more (October 26, 2026)
body: AWS Weekly Roundup: Amazon Polly Generative engine, TorchNeuron for Trainium, and more (October 26, 2026) A few weeks ago I presented to a small group of commercial and technology leaders from Brazilian agribusiness at the AWS office in São Paulo. My talk ran through where generative AI fits across the different stages of an agribusiness operation, and the point I kept returning to is that the markets we call traditional are exactly the ones where keeping up with this technology decides who ends up ahead of the curve. Nobody there was arguing about whether AI belongs in agriculture. The questions were about delivery: who receives the output, in which language, on which device, often while driving between farms. That is why a launch I might otherwise have filed under routine leads my list this week. The Amazon Polly Generative engine upgrade added 14 new voices, two of them in Brazilian Portuguese. When your user has both hands on a steering wheel, the interface is a voice. Presenting “GenAI no Agronegócio Brasileiro” at the AWS office in São Paulo. The rest of the week had a sharper edge. The biggest launch is a security service built on the premise that the gap between a vulnerability being disclosed and a vulnerability being exploited has effectively closed, and AWS published the honeypot evidence for exactly that in the same week. Now, let’s get into this week’s AWS news… AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available AWS Continuum reframes vulnerability management as an end-to-end job rather than a scanner that hands you a list. It builds a context graph from your repositories and your AWS environment, assigns each finding an evidence level, and reproduces exploitable findings in an isolated sandbox with proof-of-concept code so you see the issue rather than a severity label. It ranks issues by how close the attack path runs to business-critical systems, then opens the fix as a pull request. The control boundary matters: every remediation currently requires human approval, so you review and merge the pull request, with autonomous classes of fix gated behind confidence thresholds for the future. The “why now” came from AWS’s own honeypots in the same week. Amazon Threat Intelligence found a PHP2Shell exploitation attempt in MadPot telemetry dated October 17, four days before CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 were publicly disclosed, and on disclosure day proof-of-concept exploits were circulating around 02:00 UTC, roughly twelve hours before the embargo was due to lift at 14:00 UTC. The practical reading is direct: a patch window measured in days assumes a delay that no longer exists, and an investigation should start from the earliest known exploitation rather than from the disclosure date. AWS also published the AWS WAF mitigations for the same CVEs. Continuum is available in US East (N. Virginia) and US West (Oregon). Introducing Amazon ECS Gateway Amazon ECS Gateway splits the work of exposing a service between the people who own the network and the people who own the application. Platform teams define one gateway with the organization’s subnets, security groups, TLS certificates, listener settings, and AWS WAF web ACLs. Application teams opt in by adding a gateway connector to the service definition, and ECS gives them an ACM certificate, a unique DNS hostname, listener rules, a target group, and a security group that admits traffic only from the Application Load Balancer. The numbers make the economics clear: up to 25 services share a single ALB, ECS provisions the first ALB on first connect and removes ALBs when they are no longer needed, and a gateway can associate with up to 10,000 clusters, with five gateways per cluster. You can adopt it incrementally with UpdateService while your existing load balancer stays in place. Amazon ECS Gateway is available in all commercial Regions where Amazon ECS is available, at no additional charge. Last week’s launches Here are some launches that caught my attention this week. Nobody there was arguing about whether AI belongs in agriculture. The questions were about delivery: who receives the output, in which language, on which device, often while driving between farms. That is why a launch I might otherwise have filed under routine leads my list this week. The Amazon Polly Generative engine upgrade added 14 new voices, two of them in Brazilian Portuguese. It builds a context graph from your repositories and your AWS environment, assigns each finding an evidence level, and reproduces exploitable findings in an isolated sandbox with proof-of-concept code so you see the issue rather than a severity label. It ranks issues by how close the attack path runs to business-critical systems, then opens the fix as a pull request. The control boundary matters: every remediation currently requires human approval, so you review and merge the pull request, with autonomous classes of fix gated behind confidence thresholds for the future. The “why now” came from AWS’s own honeypots in the same week. Amazon Threat Intelligence found a PHP2Shell exploitation attempt in MadPot telemetry dated October 17, four days before CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 were publicly disclosed, and on disclosure day proof-of-concept exploits were circulating around 02:00 UTC, roughly twelve hours before the embargo was due to lift at 14:00 UTC. Platform teams define one gateway with the organization’s subnets, security groups, TLS certificates, listener settings, and AWS WAF web ACLs. title: D.C. Man Arrested for Murdering Two Youths, Ages 12 and 14
body: Press Release D.C. Man Arrested for Murdering Two Youths, Ages 12 and 14 Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia USADC.Media@usdoj.gov WASHINGTON – Antonio Terry, 18, of Washington, D.C., was arrested on October 25, 2026, and charged today with first-degree murder while armed for the shooting deaths of two youths, ages 12 and 14, that occurred on April 14, 2026, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. Judge Heide Hermann found probable cause that Terry committed the offense of first-degree murder while armed and ordered that Terry be held without bond pending a preliminary hearing scheduled for November 9, 2026. According to court documents, at approximately 3:27 p.m., on April 14, 2026, a stolen, black Honda Accord drove up to the entrance of the parking lot to the Circle 7 Express store 740 Kenilworth Avenue, Northeast. Three masked males got out of the car, opened fire on individuals in the parking lot, and then returned to the car and fled the scene. Two youths, ages 12 and 14 were shot and killed. Joining the announcement was Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll of the Metropolitan Police Department. This case is being investigated by the Metropolitan Police Department and prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Christopher Carson and Yasmin Emrani. title: Convicted Sex Offender Sentenced to 30 Years in Prison for Coercion and Enticement of a Minor and Receipt of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Convicted Sex Offender Sentenced to 30 Years in Prison for Coercion and Enticement of a Minor and Receipt of Child Pornography Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of New York Defendant Had Two Prior New York State Convictions for Sexually Assaulting Children Joseph Grunwald was sentenced yesterday by United States District Judge Nina R. Morrison to 30 years’ imprisonment for coercing and enticing a minor to engage in sexually explicit conduct, and receiving child pornography. The sentencing was held on October 22, 2026.  Grunwald pleaded guilty to a three-count superseding information in August 2026. Grunwald was a registered sex offender in New York State when he committed the federal crimes of conviction. Joseph Nocella, Jr., United States Attorney for the Eastern District of New York, and James C. Barnacle, Jr., Assistant Director in Charge, Federal Bureau of Investigation, New York Field Office (FBI), announced the sentence. “The defendant has demonstrated that he poses a grave danger to children. Today’s sentence was necessary to protect the community from this recidivist menace for decades,” stated United States Attorney Nocella.  “Notably, the defendant’s prior New York State sentences for sexually assaulting minors – in each case, he received probation – failed to deter him.” “While nothing can undo the harm suffered by the victims, this significant sentence ensures Joseph Grunwald, a convicted sex offender, will spend the next three decades unable to victimize additional children.  The FBI/NYPD Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force works day in and day out to hold accountable those who prey on children.  Individuals who choose to target the most vulnerable should take note: justice will find you,” stated FBI Assistant Director in Charge Barnacle. As set forth in court filings, between March 2023 and December 2023, Grunwald communicated over the internet and through social media with two children, John Doe-1, a 14-year-old boy, and John Doe-2, another minor boy, soliciting them both for sexually explicit videos and images.  Grunwald first contacted John Doe-1 on the messaging app Telegram, confirmed that the victim was a minor, and solicited a sexually explicit picture from him.  Grunwald was 31 years old at the time.  John Doe-1 later learned that the defendant had sent the sexually explicit picture, without the victim’s knowledge, to a group chat.  In June 2023, Grunwald began threatening the victim.  For example, on June 26, the defendant threatened:  “You’re still in trouble and remember what I said yesterday. Those boys told me something about you.”  The following day, on June 27, the defendant threatened John Doe-1 again after chasing him though the boy’s synagogue: “I am going to call your mother.  I have her cell phone number.  Good luck.  I’m going to tell her everything.” Grunwald also solicited sexually explicit pictures from John Doe-2, exchanging thousands of messages with the victim on Instagram.  Grunwald confirmed John Doe-2 was a minor, but later falsely told John Doe-2 that Grunwald was 18-years-old.  Law enforcement also seized multiple electronic devices from Grunwald containing additional child pornography in the form of pictures and videos of other minors. Grunwald was previously convicted in 2019 of sexually abusing a 7-year-old girl in a synagogue, and was sentenced to 10 years’ probation.  While the charges in that case were still pending, Grunwald sexually abused a 13-year-old boy in exchange for a cell phone and the use of the defendant’s debit card.  He pleaded guilty to misdemeanor sexual abuse and was sentenced to three years’ probation. This prosecution is part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse.  Led by United States Attorneys’ Offices, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims.  For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . The government’s case is being handled by the Office’s General Crimes Section. Assistant U.S. Attorney Vincent Chiappini is in charge of the prosecution. The Defendant : JOSEPH GRUNWALD Age:  34 Brooklyn, New York. E.D.N.Y. Docket No. 24-CR-19 (NRM) Contact John Marzulli Denise Taylor United States Attorney’s Office (718) 254-6323 Updated October 26, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - New York, Eastern

title: Canton Man Found Guilty of Child Exploitation Offense and Receipt of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Canton Man Found Guilty of Child Exploitation Offense and Receipt of Child Pornography Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov Robert Bowen, age 46, of Canton, New York, has been found guilty of sexual exploitation of a child and receipt of child pornography following a bench trial in Syracuse. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Buffalo Acting Special Agent in Charge Anthony Patrone made the announcement. Evidence presented during the bench trial proved that, in June 2025, Bowen exchanged text messages with an 8-year-old child using the Roblox application and later using his cell phone’s messaging application.  During the exchange, Bowen sent the child pornographic media and requested the child take sexually explicit images and videos of herself and send them to Bowen.  The evidence established that Bowen received sexually explicit media from the child, and requested she send more. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Sarcone stated, “Bowen used an online gaming platform, frequently visited by children to encounter and prey upon an innocent victim. Fortunately, the child’s family reported the conduct to police and Bowen was swiftly identified, thanks to the investigative efforts and successful partnership between local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies. I encourage parents and guardians to be vigilant about who their children are communicating with online. My office remains committed to protecting our communities against Internet predators such as the defendant.” “Robert Bowen’s conduct reflects the disturbing and reprehensible lengths to which some individuals will go to prey upon and exploit the most vulnerable among us” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Anthony J. Patrone of HSI Buffalo. “The exploitation of even one child is unacceptable and demands an unwavering and coordinated response. HSI Massena remains resolute in its commitment to working with our law enforcement partners across state lines to identify, apprehend and hold accountable those who harm children.” Bowen will be sentenced on February 11, 2027, by Chief United States District Judge Brenda K. Sannes, who presided over the bench trial and rendered the guilty verdicts.  The sexual exploitation of a child charge against Bowen carries a maximum sentence of 30 years in prison, a mandatory minimum sentence of 15 years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000, and a term of supervised release of at least 5 years and up to life.  The defendant will also be required to register as a sex offender.  A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the statutes the defendant violated, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines, and other factors. Homeland Security Investigations investigated the case, with assistance from the New York State Police and the Lombard, Illinois, Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Ben Gillis and Tamara Thomson are prosecuting the case. Project Safe Childhood is a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys' Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . Updated October 26, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - New York, Northern

title: New Orleans Felon Indicted for Possessing  Firearm and Ammunition
body: Press Release New Orleans Felon Indicted for Possessing  Firearm and Ammunition Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Louisiana shane.jones@usdoj.gov NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA – JOHRON WILTZ (“WILTZ”) , age 21, was indicted on October 23, 2026 for being a felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition, in violation of 18 U.S.C §§ 922(g)(1) and 924(a)(8), announced U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle. According to the indictment, on April 1, 2026, WILTZ was convicted of multiple felonies in Orleans Parish, including illegal possession of stolen things valued over $25,000. Less than two months later, on May 28, 2026, WILTZ was arrested in possession of a Glock Model 19 firearm and additional ammunition. As to both offenses, WILTZ faces up to 15 years in prison, up to a $250,000 fine, and up to three years of supervised release. Each count also carries a mandatory $100 special assessment fee. U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle reiterated that the indictment is merely an allegation and that the guilt of the defendant must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt. The case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and Louisiana Probation and Parole. Assistant United States Attorney David Berman of the Violent Crime Unit is in charge of the prosecution. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. *** Contact Shane M. Sarcone III and Anthony Patrone, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the Buffalo Field Office of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI). As part of his guilty plea, Schreck admitted that in December of 1997, he was convicted under New York state law of two counts of sodomy in the second degree. Schreck also admitted that in February of 2026, he possessed a cell phone and a tablet on which Schreck possessed numerous images and videos of child pornography, including material depicting the sexual abuse of children as young as two years old. Due to Schreck’s prior New York state conviction, at sentencing, Schreck faces a mandatory minimum term of 10 years in federal prison and a statutory maximum of 20 years. Schreck also faces a fine of up to $250,000, and a term of supervised release of at least 5 years and up to life.  Schreck will also be required to register as a sex offender upon his release from prison. A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statutes the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors. Sentencing is currently scheduled for February 5, 2027, at 11:00 am in Syracuse, New York, before Chief U.S. District Judge, Brenda K. Sannes. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Sarcone stated, “This defendant’s recidivism has landed him back in jail, this time, for 10 to 20 years. Our priority is to find and prosecute anyone who victimizes children whether that be through hands-on abuse or through the trafficking and possession of child pornography. Our children deserve to be protected and we remain dedicated, as do our law enforcement partners, to doing whatever we can to ensure they are.” “This defendant’s prior conviction for sexually abusing a child and his subsequent possession of child sexual abuse material demonstrate the ongoing danger posed by repeat offenders,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Anthony Patrone of HSI Buffalo. “HSI Syracuse is committed to holding repeat offenders accountable, protecting the most vulnerable members of our communities, and ensuring that those who exploit children face the full consequences of their actions.” HSI is investigating the case with assistance from the New York State Police. title: U.S. Attorney’s Office announces 2026 Election Integrity Plan for general election and early voting in Kansas
body: Press Release U.S. Attorney’s Office announces 2026 Election Integrity Plan for general election and early voting in Kansas Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Kansas KANSAS CITY, KAN. – The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Kansas (USAO-KS), in coordination with the Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division , unveils its comprehensive strategy to oversee federal voting protections and investigate potential election fraud as early voting begins in Kansas for the 2026 midterm elections . “President Abraham Lincoln said it best when he said we are a ‘government of the people, by the people, for the people’,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser. “Voting gives American citizens a voice in their government, and fair elections are the heart of our democratic republic. Our office will work to ensure that Kansans can cast their ballots without fear or worry that voting results will be tainted by fraud, intimidation, or illegal ballots.” The initiative is part of a nationwide effort to ensure a secure, transparent, and accessible voting process. The U.S. Attorney’s Office, alongside federal law enforcement partners, is prepared to enforce federal election laws vigorously while protecting the right of every legal voter to cast their ballot without intimidation or interference. Voters can consult official Department of Justice and state portals to review federal election laws and eligibility requirements. Key Enforcement Priorities for the 2026 Election: • Protecting Voter Rights : Ensuring that all eligible voters can participate in early voting, mail-in voting, and Election Day voting free from discrimination, harassment, or unlawful coercion. • Ensuring Voter Eligibility and Enforcement : Monitoring compliance with federal laws regarding voter registration and eligibility. For detailed information on ongoing reviews, eligibility laws, or federal penalties, please consult official Department of Justice guidelines and state election authority resources. • Combating Election Fraud : Investigating actionable allegations of ballot harvesting, voter impersonation, or intentional disruption of polling places and mail-in ballot processing. Mail-In and Early Voting in Kansas Kansas state election officials have confirmed that early in-person voting and mail-in voting have begun. Federal oversight will remain active throughout the early voting period to monitor compliance with the Voting Rights Act and ensure that secure ballot drop boxes and polling locations are unhindered. Reporting Election Irregularities Assistant U.S. Attorney/District Election Officer Jared Maag will be on duty in this District while the polls are open. He can be reached by the public at (785) 295-2850. The public plays a critical role in maintaining election security. Anyone who witnesses or has direct knowledge of potential election fraud, voter intimidation, or unlawful voting activity is strongly encouraged to report it immediately. You can also visit the official FBI Tips Portal to report potential election fraud or voting irregularities. Complaints regarding voter discrimination or civil rights violations can also be directed to the Civil Rights Division via the Department of Justice Civil Rights Reporting Portal . Please note, however, in the case of a crime of violence or intimidation, call 911 immediately and before contacting federal authorities. State and local police have primary jurisdiction over polling places, and almost always have faster reaction capacity in an emergency. ### Updated October 26, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Component USAO - Kansas

title: Syracuse Man Charged with Making Threats Against the President
body: Press Release Syracuse Man Charged with Making Threats Against the President Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov Christopher Vignogna, age 26, of Syracuse, New York, appeared in Federal Court Friday, October 9, 2026, on a charge of making threats against the President of the United States. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and United States Secret Service, Special Agent in Charge Charles T. Perras made the announcement. The complaint filed against Vignogna alleges that on October 7, 2026, Vignogna asked a co-worker to inquire if her boyfriend could buy Vignogna a gun so he could shoot the President at a rally in Syracuse on October 9, 2026.  The complaint alleges that Vignogna also stated that Trump is coming to Syracuse and I want to shoot him. The charge filed against Vignogna carries a maximum sentence of 5 years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000, and a term of supervised release of up to 3 years.  A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statute(s) the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors. Vignogna was arraigned before United States Magistrate Judge Mitchell J. Katz and released on conditions pending a trial. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III stated, “I want to commend the U.S. Secret Service for their swift and immediate response to this serious conduct.  May this arrest serve as a deterrent to others who think it is acceptable to threaten the President of the United States.  It will not be tolerated on my watch.” United States Secret Service, Special Agent in Charge Charles T. Perras said, “The United States Secret Service reaffirms that the safety and security of our protectees remains our highest priority. Every potential threat is taken seriously, investigated thoroughly, and pursued with the full intention of bringing individuals who violate the law to justice.  This mission is not accomplished alone. Collaboration with our state, local, and federal partners is essential to ensuring swift and successful protective and investigative operations. The Secret Service extends its appreciation to the U.S. Attorney’s Office, Northern District of New York, the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albany Office, and the Onondaga County Sheriff’s Office for their continued support and cooperation.” The charges in the complaint are merely accusations. The defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. This case is being investigated by the United States Secret Service. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael Whalen. Updated October 26, 2026 Topic National Security Component USAO - New York, Northern

body: Press Release Broome County Trio Arrested in Large Scale Meth Ring Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov On October 2, 2026, Jermaine Cooper, age 53, of Apalachin, NY; Sherry Olk, age 40, of Binghamton, NY; and Shamell Tate, age 36 of Endicott, NY, were arraigned on charges of distribution of methamphetamine. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III, FBI Special Agent in Charge Craig Tremaroli, Broome County District Attorney F. Paul Battisti, Broome County Sheriff Frederick J. Akshar II, New York State Police (NYSP) Bureau of Criminal Investigation Lieutenant Nate McCarthy, and Vestal Police Chief Vince Stavola made the announcement. The complaint against Cooper and Olk, alleges the two sold over 100 grams of a mixture and substance containing methamphetamine in July 2026.  A separate complaint against Tate alleges in September 2026, he sold over 200 grams of a mixture and substance containing methamphetamine. These charges carry a mandatory minimum sentence of 5 years in prison, a maximum sentence of 40 years in prison, a fine up to $250,000, and a term of supervised release of at least 5 years and up to life.  A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statute(s) the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors. All defendants are currently detaining pending a trial before a United States District Court. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III stated, “These three drug dealers have been exploiting drug addiction for their financial gain and infiltrating deadly narcotics into our community for far too long. New York’s bail reform laws would have allowed these defendants right back on the street after arraignment, and my office will continue to use federal laws to remove drug traffickers from the community and safeguard the Southern Tier. These arrests should serve as a chilly reminder that if you are poisoning our communities with narcotics, we will find you and bring the fullest extent of the federal government to your doorstep.” “These arrests and seizures are a direct result of the continued partnerships and incredible coordination we share at every level of law enforcement throughout Broome County,” said Craig Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albany Field Office. “As alleged, these subjects were making a living off bringing dangerous drugs into our communities, not caring how it was hurting our neighbors. But law enforcement cares, and now they are all facing potential time in federal prison. The FBI remains deeply committed to working with our partner agencies to aggressively investigate drug traffickers and ensure they are sent to prison.” Broome County District Attorney Paul Battisti stated, “This coordinated effort demonstrates the effectiveness of multi-agency collaboration in tackling drug-related crimes. No longer are the days of federal, state and local law enforcement agencies working in silos. As has been demonstrated with Clean Sweep in April and again today with Cold Front, we are One Team, laser focused on the safety and security of our community and will stop at nothing when public safety is at risk.” “Getting dangerous drug dealers off our streets is what the law-abiding residents and families of our community expect and deserve from law enforcement,” said Broome County Sheriff Fred Akshar.  “It takes coordination, cooperation and teamwork at every level to build a safer Broome County and to put the peddlers of poison where they belong, behind bars and unable to create new victims.” NYSP Bureau of Criminal Investigation Lieutenant Nate McCarthy stated, “I would like to thank all of the law enforcement professional that touched this case, including many of our agencies’ civilian support staff.  Each member contributed to this investigation, leading to its success. These cases demand extensive investigative expertise, coordination, and countless hours of work.  The results speak for themselves and are a direct reflection of the commitment and strength of our continued partnerships.” Vestel Police Chief Vince Stavola stated, “This case reinforces that effective interagency partnerships are essential to addressing public safety and protecting the communities we serve. By sharing resources, maintaining open lines of communication, and working toward a common goal, we can collectively achieve better outcomes and improve public safety not only in the Town of Vestal, but throughout our surrounding communities.” The charges in the complaint are merely accusations. The defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. FBI, NYSP, Broome County Sheriff’s Office and Vestal Police Department are investigating the case. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kristen Grabowski and Michael Whalen are prosecuting the case. title: Maryland Man Pleads Guilty to Burning Commercial Establishment
body: Press Release Maryland Man Pleads Guilty to Burning Commercial Establishment Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Maryland Greenbelt, Maryland – A Maryland man pled guilty to arson in federal court, today, stemming from an incident in which he set fire to a commercial building. Shawn Justice, 38, of Avenue, pled guilty to one count of arson. Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the guilty plea with Special Agent in Charge Charles Doerrer, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF), and Chief Caroll H. Spriggs, II, Office of the Maryland State Fire Marshal. According to his guilty plea, on October 29, 2025, Justice entered Pasha Lounge, a bar and Hookah establishment in Waldorf, Maryland, through the front door and went to a humidor.  Justice then went inside of the humidor where he scattered cigars on the ground, poured liquor over them, lit a paper towel roll on fire, and then tossed the flaming paper-towel roll on the floor littered with alcohol-soaked cigars.  The humidor burst into flames, resulting in the lounge incurring more than $80,000 in losses. Justice faces a maximum of 20 years in federal prison for arson.  U.S. District Judge Theodore J. Chuang scheduled sentencing for Friday, Mar. 5, 2027, at 2:30 p.m. Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. A federal district judge determines sentencing after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. U.S. Attorney Hayes commended the ATF and Office of the Maryland State Fire Marshal for their work in the investigation. U.S. Attorney Hayes also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorney Alex Treiger who is prosecuting this case. For more information about the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office, its priorities, and resources available to help the community, visit justice.gov/usao-md . # # # Contact Kevin Nash USAMD.Press@usdoj.gov 410-209-4946 Updated October 26, 2026 Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - Maryland

title: Illegal Immigrant from Mexico Pleads Guilty to Staging Fake Kidnapping Last Year Purportedly Committed by Federal Agents
body: Press Release Illegal Immigrant from Mexico Pleads Guilty to Staging Fake Kidnapping Last Year Purportedly Committed by Federal Agents Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Central District of California LOS ANGELES – An illegal alien from Mexico pleaded guilty today to orchestrating a phony kidnapping last year that she blamed on federal agents or people working with federal agents. Yuriana Julia Pelaez Calderón, 43, of South Los Angeles, pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to impede, obstruct, impair, and defeat the lawful function of Homeland Security Investigations within federal jurisdiction. According to her plea agreement, in June 2025, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) was engaged in carrying out lawful government functions, including credible threats to public safety such as kidnapping. In June and July of 2025, Calderón faked her apprehension by federal agents or surrogates acting on behalf of federal agents. On June 25, 2025, Calderón falsely told an individual that “immigration” was taking her while in or near a fast-food restaurant and that immigration officials had “turned the lights on,” “threatened to break her window” and were taking her into custody, according to court documents. Two days later, Calderón called another individual, who was a member of a tenants’ rights group, using the caller ID blocking feature on her telephone and falsely claimed she had been taken by “authorities” to San Ysidro where Calderón and others were pressured to sign voluntary removal documents. That same day, Calderón called a third individual, again using the caller ID blocking feature on her phone, and falsely claimed that she had been moved to a warehouse in an unknown location where she was being held with other detainees. On June 28, 2025, Calderón made another phone call to the second individual she contacted, using her caller ID blocking phone feature, and said she was being held with someone from “B-18” (an immigration facility in Los Angeles) and another person who had been “picked up at a gas station in Bakersfield.” As a result of Calderón’s intentional lies, false information was reported to the media and law enforcement that Calderón had been “kidnapped” by masked men in plain clothes driving an unmarked vehicle, who were acting as federal agents or as surrogates of federal agents. On June 30, 2025, in Los Angeles, community organizers held a press conference where other individuals repeated Calderón’s lies and demanded her “release” from custody. Meanwhile, Calderón knew about the false media coverage and chose to stay hidden in Bakersfield. On July 3, 2025, Calderón used the caller ID blocking feature on her phone again called an individual and falsely claimed she would be released soon because of all the media coverage. That same day, she traveled from Bakersfield to Tulare County to stage her release from custody. She then approached an individual in Tulare County and lied that she had just been dropped off by “Border Patrol.” She then asked this individual to be a witness in her “case” against “Border Patrol” because she planned to sue that agency. Calderón also altered her appearance to make it appear that she had been mistreated while in custody. A co-conspirator took photographs of Calderón’s altered appearance. From July 3, 2025, to July 5, 2025, Calderón turned off her phones and refused to return the phone calls of law enforcement officials, and caused others to do the same, when she knew law enforcement was looking for her. Calderón knew or had reason to know that law enforcement would expend resources looking for her because of her false kidnapping claims. United States District Judge Stephen V. Wilson scheduled a February 8, 2027, sentencing hearing, at which time Calderón will face a statutory maximum sentence of five years in federal prison. HSI’s El Camino Real Financial Crimes Division, a multi-agency division of HSI Los Angeles that includes federal and state investigators, investigated this matter. Assistant United States Attorneys Lana Morton Owens of the National Security Division and Matthew J. Tako of the Transnational Organized Crime Section are prosecuting this case. title: Honduran Illegal Alien Indicted for Attempted Coercion and Enticement of A Minor and Illegal Reentry of A Removed Alien
body: Press Release Honduran Illegal Alien Indicted for Attempted Coercion and Enticement of A Minor and Illegal Reentry of A Removed Alien Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Louisiana shane.jones@usdoj.gov NEW ORLEANS – LESLI JOEL CALIX-SARMIENTO (“CALIX-SARMIENTO”) , age 36, a Honduran national, was charged in a two-count indictment on October 23, 2026, with attempted coercion and enticement of a minor, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Section 2422(b), and illegal reentry of a removed alien, in violation of Title 8, United States Code, Section 1326(a), announced U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle. According to Count 1 of the indictment, between August 27, 2026, and August 28, 2026, CALIX-SARMIENTO persuaded and enticed an individual he believed to be a fifteen-year-old female to engage in illegal and illicit sexual activity. In addition, on or about August 28, 2026, CALIX-SARMIENTO , an alien, was found in the United States after having been deported and removed therefrom on or about August 27, 2013, February 11, 2014, and March 11, 2014, without the approval of the Attorney General of the United States, or his designated successor, the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security, having expressly consented to the defendant’s reapplication for admission into the United States. Through a partnership between state and federal authorities, the U.S. Attorney’s Office adopted the state charges, and is now federally prosecuting CALIX-SARMIENTO . If convicted of Count 1, CALIX-SARMIENTO faces a mandatory minimum of ten (10) years and up to a lifetime in prison, at least five (5) years and up to a lifetime of supervised release, as well as  sex offender registration. If convicted of  Count 2, CALIX-SARMIENTO faces up to two (2) years imprisonment, and up to one (1) year of supervised release.  As to each count, CALIX-SARMIENTO also faces up to a $250,000 fine and a $100 mandatory special assessment fee. U. S. Attorney Courcelle reiterated that the indictment is merely a charge and that the guilt of the defendant must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt. U.S. Attorney Courcelle praised the work of the Homeland Security Investigations, Louisiana Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force and the Assumption Parish Sheriff’s Department in investigating this matter. Assistant United States Attorney Mary Anne Flippo of the Public Integrity Unit and Human Trafficking and Child Exploitation Task Force is in charge of the prosecution. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.projectsafechildhood.gov . *     *    * Contact Shane M. Oswego Man Charged with Sexual Exploitation of a Child and Transportation and Possession of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Oswego Man Charged with Sexual Exploitation of a Child and Transportation and Possession of Child Pornography Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov On October 9, 2026, Emerardo Abisai Vasquez-Lopez, age 20, of Oswego, New York, appeared in federal court in Syracuse, New York, before United States Magistrate Judge Mitchell J. Katz on charges related to his alleged sexual exploitation of a child and his transportation and possession of child pornography. Vasquez-Lopez was ordered detained pending further proceedings. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Anthony Patrone, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the Buffalo Field Office of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), made the announcement. The complaint filed against Vasquez-Lopez alleges that between August and October of 2024, Vasquez-Lopez sexually abused a 9-year-old child and created images and videos of that abuse. Following the abuse, Vasquez-Lopez uploaded the material he created to a cloud storage account under his control. Vasquez-Lopez also downloaded child pornography from the same cloud storage account and possessed some of that material on an electronic device belonging to him that was seized at the time of his arrest. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Sarcone stated, “This defendant’s abuse of a vulnerable child coupled with his creation of images and videos memorializing that abuse is absolutely reprehensible. The swift actions taken by HSI and the New York State Police to find and detain the defendant has ensured that while these charges are pending, he will be behind bars and cannot pray on children and endanger our community.” “Sexual abuse and the creation and sharing of child sexual abuse material inflict profound and lasting harm on children, their families and the communities that depend on adults to protect them,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Anthony Patrone of HSI Buffalo. “These alleged acts betray the trust and safety every child deserves, while the continued circulation of such material extends the victimization and endangers the public. HSI Syracuse works every day with our law enforcement partners to identify those who target and exploit vulnerable children, safeguard victims and hold offenders accountable." The sexual exploitation charge filed against Vasquez-Lopez carries a term of 15 to 30 years in federal prison. The transportation charge carries a term of five to 20 years in federal prison. The possession charge carries a term of up to 20 years in federal prison. Each count carries a fine of up to $250,000 and a term of supervised release of at least 5 years and up to life.  If convicted, Vasquez-Lopez will also be required to register as a sex offender upon his release from prison and may ultimately be deported and removed from the United States based on his lack of lawful status. A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statutes the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors. The charges in the complaint are merely accusations. The defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. HSI and the New York State Police are investigating the case. The case is being prosecuted by Adrian LaRochelle as part of Project Safe Childhood. Project Safe Childhood is a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. title: Federal agents arrest former CEO of child & adolescent residential treatment center on federal child pornography, coercion charges
body: Press Release Federal agents arrest former CEO of child & adolescent residential treatment center on federal child pornography, coercion charges Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Ohio COLUMBUS, Ohio – The former CEO of a Belmont County residential treatment facility for children and adolescents was arrested by federal agents on child pornography and coercion charges. Randall J. MacKendrick, 59, of St. Clairsville, was arrested in August on local charges after attempting to meet up with who he believed was a teenage girl. One month later, while out on bond, MacKendrick was re-arrested for being in contact with a minor female who was a former patient at the treatment center. In October, the FBI learned MacKendrick is a suspect in a May kidnapping and rape of a 14-year-old female in Perry County. MacKendrick served as the CEO of Fox Run Center for Children and Adolescents in St. Clairsville. The facility treats boys ages 5 to 12 and girls ages 12 to 17. He appeared in federal court in Columbus this afternoon for an initial appearance, and his federal charges were unsealed at that time. According to the charging documents, in June 2026, MacKendrick began communicating online with a North Ridgeville police officer acting undercover and posing as a 14-year-old female. MacKendrick allegedly communicated with who he believed was a teenage girl until August 2026, sending the undercover officer sexually explicit messages, offering to send gifts and requesting to meet in person. It is alleged that MacKendrick traveled to central Ohio in July 2026 attempting to meet up with the fictitious teenager at Polaris Fashion Place, Tanger Outlets and a Holiday Inn. In August, MacKendrick allegedly traveled to South Central Park in Lorain County to meet up with the purported teenager. MacKendrick was arrested on local charges after departing the park. In his vehicle, law enforcement found multiple sex toys, several condoms and three cell phones. Also in August, Belmont County Sheriff’s Office detectives searched MacKendrick’s office and residence. During their forensic analysis of MacKendrick’s digital devices, deputies discovered images and videos of child sexual abuse material. MacKendrick was released on bond in his local case but was re-arrested in September, when law enforcement officers learned MacKendrick was allegedly in contact with a former patient of Fox Run who is 17 years old. MacKendrick’s bond was increased and he was released again. In October, FBI agents learned MacKendrick is a suspect in a Perry County case involving the kidnapping and rape of a 14-year-old. MacKendrick’s DNA matches DNA recovered from the victim. That investigation is still ongoing. MacKendrick was arrested Saturday in West Virginia and transferred to the Southern District of Ohio prior to today’s initial appearance. The defendant is charged with possessing child pornography, a federal crime punishable by up to 20 years in prison, and attempted coercion and enticement of a minor, which carries a potential penalty of at least 10 years and up to life in prison. Dominick S. Gerace II, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Ohio; Jason Cromartie, Special Agent in Charge, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Cincinnati Division; the North Ridgeville Police Department; and Belmont County Sheriff James G. Zusack announced the charges. Assistant United States Attorneys Emily Czerniejewski and Tyler J. Aagard are representing the United States in this case. A criminal complaint merely contains allegations, and defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law. This case is part of Project Safe Childhood , a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by U.S. Attorney’s Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. # # # Updated October 26, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Ohio, Southern

title: New York Woman Charged With $1.1M Check Cashing Scheme
body: Press Release New York Woman Charged With $1.1M Check Cashing Scheme Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Xue Fang Cheng, 55, of New York, was arrested today after a federal grand jury in the Eastern District of New York returned an indictment on Oct. 23 charging Cheng with providing illegal check cashing services. According to court documents, Cheng was an owner of a New York convenience store that provided unlicensed check cashing services to at least three individuals, including a social adult day care center owner and an undercover law enforcement agent. Cheng directed that checks be deposited in business bank accounts held by various companies and controlled by others, and she provided cash to her customers for a 2–3% fee. Cheng documented the cashed checks via text and audio messages and instructed the undercover agent that they should “plan to do [it] long term,” cautioning that “[i]t is very dangerous.” From March 2025 through July 2026, Cheng allegedly participated in providing over $1.1 million in cash to her customers. In connection with the investigation, law enforcement seized approximately $875,000. Cheng is charged with conspiracy to operate an unlicensed money transmitting business. If convicted, she faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division; U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella, Jr. for the Eastern District of New York; Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda L. Bennett of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG); Pete Gizas, Acting Special Agent in Charge, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) New York; and Jessica S. Tisch, Commissioner, New York City Police Department (NYPD), made the announcement. HHS-OIG, HSI New York, and the NYPD are investigating the case. Deputy Chief Patrick J. Campbell and Trial Attorney Leonid Sandlar of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section are prosecuting the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit . An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. title: Public Company Officers Plead Guilty to International Securities Fraud Conspiracies
body: Press Release Public Company Officers Plead Guilty to International Securities Fraud Conspiracies Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Georgia ATLANTA – Zoltan Nagy, a Canadian businessman, and Glenn Laken, an Illinois trader previously convicted of federal securities fraud and racketeering offenses, have pleaded guilty to conspiring to commit securities fraud in connection with international pump-and-dump schemes that resulted in over $1 million in losses. Three Canadian co-conspirators, Phillip Sewell, Richard Tang, and Davies Wong, previously pleaded guilty to similar charges. “These defendants engaged in sophisticated stock price manipulation that harmed investors and undermined confidence in the market,” said U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg. “With the assistance of our partners in law enforcement and at the Securities and Exchange Commission, we will continue to aggressively root out and prosecute criminals who perpetrate securities fraud.” “These defendants manipulated the stock market for their own financial gain, exploiting investors and compromising the security of brokerage accounts to carry out their schemes,” said Marlo Graham, Special Agent in Charge of FBI Atlanta. “These guilty pleas underscore the FBI’s commitment to working with our law enforcement partners to investigate complex financial crimes, hold those responsible accountable, and protect the integrity of our financial markets.” According to U.S. Attorney Hertzberg, the indictment, and other information presented in court: Nagy and Laken were the majority shareholders of two different publicly traded penny stock companies at the heart of separate, but substantially similar, pump-and-dump schemes. Both schemes involved hacking U.S.-based online consumer brokerage accounts and forcing purchases of worthless penny stocks that Nagy’s and Laken’s co-conspirators controlled. The Lotus Scheme Nagy was the sole officer and director of Lotus Bio-Technology Development Corp. (“Lotus”), a penny stock company that traded publicly under the ticker LBTD. By the beginning of August 2017, Nagy, Tang, Wong, and Sewell controlled the vast bulk of outstanding LBTD shares that were available for public trading. On August 16, 2017, Rahim Mohamed, another co-conspirator, or someone acting at his direction, allegedly hacked into a U.S.-based online brokerage account and forced it to purchase 200,000 LBTD shares. At almost the same time, Wong and other co-conspirators sold approximately 261,000 LBTD shares, the majority of which were ultimately purchased by the hacked brokerage account at inflated prices. On September 19, 2017, the co-conspirators struck again, on a significantly larger scale. Mohamed, or others acting at his direction, allegedly hacked into 24 customer accounts at multiple U.S.-based online brokerage firms and forced them to purchase millions of LBTD shares. While the compromised accounts were forced to buy LBTD shares, Wong and other co-conspirators sold approximately 7.75 million LBTD shares for nearly $1.1 million in proceeds. In the weeks that followed, the proceeds from these sales were divided between Nagy, Wong, Tang, Mohamed, Sewell, and others. The Good Gaming Scheme Laken was the CEO, chairman, and controlling shareholder of a publicly traded company that, by late 2017, owned 61% of Good Gaming, Inc., a penny stock company that traded publicly under the ticker GMER. In 2002, Laken was convicted of racketeering conspiracy, wire fraud, and other federal charges related to a pension fund fraud and conspiracy to commit securities and wire fraud related to a stock manipulation scheme. Between January 12 and January 18, 2018, Tang coordinated with Laken to transfer approximately 2.9 million GMER shares to accounts held by co-conspirators. On January 22, 2018, Mohamed, or others acting at his direction, allegedly hacked into several accounts at U.S.-based online brokerage firms and forced them to purchase more than one million GMER shares. At the same time, other co-conspirators sold more than 700,000 of the GMER shares they had originally obtained from Laken for nearly $170,000. The proceeds were then divided between Laken, Tang, Mohamed, and other co-conspirators. On October 20, 2026, Zoltan Nagy, 60, of Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit securities fraud. His sentencing hearing is set for January 20, 2027, at 2:00 p.m. before U.S. District Judge Victoria M. Calvert. On September 25, 2026, Glenn Laken, 72, of Chicago, Illinois, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit securities fraud. His sentencing hearing is set for January 13, 2027, at 11:00 a.m. Sewell, Tang, and Wong previously pleaded guilty for their involvement in the Lotus Scheme: On September 17, 2024, Phillip Sewell, 65, of Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit securities fraud. His sentencing hearing is set for January 22, 2027, at 10:30 a.m. On October 23, 2024, Richard Tang, 49, of Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud. His sentencing hearing is set for January 21, 2027, at 10:30 a.m. On November 29, 2023, Davies Wong, 67, of Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit securities fraud. His sentencing hearing is set for January 21, 2027, at 1:30 p.m. Tang faces up to twenty years’ imprisonment, and Laken, Nagy, Sewell, and Wong face up to five years’ imprisonment. Each defendant also may be ordered to pay restitution to the victims and a fine of up to $250,000 or twice the gain or loss amount, whichever is greater. In determining the actual sentence, the Court will consider the United States Sentencing Guidelines, which are not binding but provide appropriate sentencing ranges for most offenders. Rahim Mohamed, 50, of Calgary, Alberta, Canada is still at large. Information regarding his whereabouts should be reported to local law enforcement. This case is being investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation with substantial assistance from the Securities and Exchange Commission. Assistant United States Attorneys Benjamin Wylly, Adam Sunstrom, and Samir Kaushal are prosecuting the case. First Assistant United States Attorney Nathan P. Kitchens and former Assistant United States Attorneys Tal C. Chaiken, Alex R. Sistla, and Christopher J. Huber previously prosecuted the case. For further information please contact the U.S. Attorney’s Public Affairs Office at USAGAN.PressEmails@usdoj.gov or (404) 581-6185. The Internet address for the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia is http://www.justice.gov/usao-ndga . "The victims in these cases deserve swift justice, and this FBI stands ready to deliver that to them so they can focus on rebuilding their lives.” This case was investigated by the FBI’s Albany Division Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force and the New York State Police with assistance from the Waverly New York Police Department and the Broome County Sheriff’s Office. title: DC Man Pleads Guilty to Escaping from Baltimore Correctional Facility
body: Press Release DC Man Pleads Guilty to Escaping from Baltimore Correctional Facility Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Maryland Baltimore, Maryland – A Washington, DC man pled guilty in federal court, today, to charges stemming from his escape from a Baltimore correctional facility. Lamont Antwan Warren, 46, pled guilty to escape from custody. Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the guilty plea with Clinton J. Fuchs, U.S. Marshal for the District of Maryland (USMS). According to his guilty plea, in May 2025, while serving a five-year sentence for sex-abuse crimes, Warren escaped from a Baltimore Volunteer of America’s Residential Re-Entry Center (RRC). On May 22, authorities transferred Warren from a Waymart, Pennsylvania correctional facility to Baltimore to serve the remainder of his sentence in community housing. Additionally, due to relocating, Warren was required to register as a sex offender in Maryland within three days of his arrival. One day after his transfer, RRC staff found Warren under the influence of an unknown drug. Law enforcement searched Warren and discovered unknown narcotics in his possession. RRC staff then attempted to require Warren to meet with his case worker. But instead, Warren ignored directives, refused to meet with his case worker, and then exited the facility. Two minutes later, RRC staff received an alert that Warren tampered with his GPS monitor. Staff then discovered the device in the RRC’s parking lot. Before Warren escaped, he did not register as a sex offender. Then on June 25, 2025, authorities found and apprehended Warren in Washington, DC. If convicted, Warren faces a maximum sentence of five years in prison for escape from custody. Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. A federal district court judge determines sentencing after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. U.S. Attorney Hayes commended USMS for its work in the investigation. Ms. Hayes also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorney Alexandria A. Bell who is prosecuting the federal case. For more information about the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office, its priorities, and resources available to help the community, visit justice.gov/usao-md . # # # Contact Kevin Nash USAMD.Press@usdoj.gov 410-209-4946 Updated October 26, 2026 Components USAO - Maryland U.S. Marshals Service

title: Scotia Man Pleads Guity to Attempted Coercion and Enticement of a Minor and Possession of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Scotia Man Pleads Guity to Attempted Coercion and Enticement of a Minor and Possession of Child Pornography Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov On October 19, 2026, Zachary Long, age 27, of Scotia, New York, pled guilty before United States District Judge Mae A. D’Agostino to attempted online coercion and enticement of a minor and possession of child pornography. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Craig L. Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Albany Field Office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), made the announcement. During his plea, Long admitted that between August 22 and September 27, 2023, he exchanged text messages with someone he believed to be the uncle of a 10-year-old boy.  In these messages, Long expressed interest in engaging in sexual activity with the minor child.  On September 27, 2023, Long arrived at a pre-determined location to engage in sex acts with the child and was arrested by law enforcement.  Long also admitted to possessing child pornography on his cellular phone. At sentencing set for February 19, 2027, Long will receive a sentence of at least 10 years and up to life in prison, be placed on supervised release after serving his term of imprisonment for at least five years and up to life, could be fined up to $250,000, and will be required to forfeit to the government the property he used to commit the offenses. In addition, Long will have to register as a sex offender. A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statutes the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines, and other factors. First Assistant United States Attorney Sarcone said: “My Office will always prioritize the investigation and prosecution of individuals who commit or try to commit sex crimes against children. I thank the FBI, the New York State Police, and the Colonie Police Department for their diligent investigation.” “Mr. Long admitted to making plans to engage in sex acts with a child he believed was 10-year-old,” said Craig Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albany Field Office. “Now, his only plans for at least the next decade will include sitting behind bars in federal prison. The FBI’s Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force will continue to work around the clock to aggressively investigate child predators who seek to harm our most vulnerable and ensure they end up in prison.” This case is being investigated by the FBI and its Child Exploitation Task Force, which includes members of federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies, including the New York State Police and Colonie Police Department.  Assistant United States Attorney A.J. Vickey is prosecuting the case as part of Project Safe Childhood. Project Safe Childhood is a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys' Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . Updated October 26, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - New York, Northern
